title: Policy adjudicator refactor for geo-tier fallbacks and model-variant routing
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Refactor the policy adjudicator to provide a single, testable validation + runtime decision component for region selection, tier routing, and fallback model variants. Current problem: routing decisions are scattered between the policy compiler, runtime dispatch, and a brittle validator that misses cross-field invariants (e.g., tier->region mappings + allowed fallback variants). This causes production surprises when we roll out new model variants or add regional capacity constraints.

Scope: Design and implement a typed adjudicator that consumes routing DSL AST (post-parse), runs staged validations (schema, semantic, cost/latency guardrails), and emits a compact decision plan used by the runtime. The adjudicator must support:
- Declarative region constraints (include/exclude lists, capacity thresholds)
- Tier affinity and hard/soft priorities (e.g., prefer-dedicated > shared > fallback)
- Model variant fallbacks with compatibility checks (input/output contract + quantization compatibility)
- Backward compatibility shims for legacy routing fields
- A migration path (lint + automated fix suggestions) for existing policies

Planned approach:
1) Define a minimal typed IR for adjudication (fields: selector, region_rules, tier_rules, fallback_graph, safety_constraints). Keep IR flat and serializable for easy unit testing.
2) Implement staged validators: schema -> semantic (cross-field) -> constraint-sim (run short path permutations to detect dead-ends).
3) Add a 'safety mode' runtime flag: in conservative mode, only allow fallbacks that maintain latency SLOs and token-cost bounds.
4) Build property-based fuzz tests (QuickCheck-style) and a corpus of real policies from prod (anonymized) to validate validator coverage.
5) Create migration linter that surfaces failing policies and auto-proposes fixes (PRs + CLI autofix).

Success criteria / acceptance:
- Adjudicator unit tests cover 95% of the policy fuzz corpus edge cases.
- No routing regressions during canary: <0.5% increase in 95p latency for routes using fallback variants.
- Migration linter finds >80% of prod policies with missing explicit fallbacks and produces valid autofix in safe cases.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Large policy surface may hide semantic assumptions. Mitigation: incremental rollout and provide runtime fallback to legacy compiler if adjudicator errors.
- Risk: Performance overhead of decision plan generation. Mitigation: cache compiled decision plans and only revalidate on policy change.
